name: Insulation
summary: Materials that slow heat loss: glass and mineral wool, foam board, spray foam and reflective foil.
uses: Insulating a shelter, room or sleeping area
Building a cooler, hay-box cooker or solar oven
Wrapping pipes and tanks against freezing
identify: Lofts and wall cavities, foam boards on building sites, foam inside fridges, freezers, coolers and water heaters, and foil on HVAC ducts. In old buildings, grey-brown granular loose fill (vermiculite) and old pipe lagging may contain asbestos: leave them alone. Plastic foam burns fast with thick, toxic smoke: cover it and keep it away from stoves and heaters.
test: Dry, fluffy and clean is good; wet, squashed or mouldy insulation has lost most of its value. Wear gloves, long sleeves and a mask for glass wool.

decay.note: Lasts if dry. Wet insulation is useless and grows mould.
